content_voiceover: This slide covers juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, or JMMoL, a rare and aggressive myeloid neoplasm of early childhood that sits in the overlap category of myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative neoplasms, MDS slash MPN. Diagnosis relies on three categories of criteria. Category one lists mandatory clinical and hematologic features, and all of them must be present: a peripheral blood monocyte count greater than 1 times ten to the ninth per liter, blasts in peripheral blood and bone marrow under 20 percent, splenomegaly, and absence of the t(9;22) BCR-ABL fusion gene, which rules out chronic myeloid leukemia. Category two covers molecular diagnostics, and only one of these needs to be present: a somatic mutation in PTPN11, KRAS, or NRAS; a clinical diagnosis of neurofibromatosis type 1 or a germline NF1 mutation; or a germline CBL mutation with loss of heterozygosity of CBL. Category three lists additional supportive hematologic features, and at least two are required only if none of the category two molecular criteria are met; these include monosomy 7 or another clonal cytogenetic abnormality, increased fetal hemoglobin for age, circulating myeloid precursors on the peripheral smear, white blood cell count over 10 times ten to the ninth per liter, granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor hypersensitivity in a colony assay, and hyperphosphorylation of STAT5. Pathogenesis centers on a hyperactive RAS signaling pathway, which makes sense given that PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, NF1, and CBL are all RAS pathway genes. Prognosis is variable: about one third of patients have aggressive disease with rapid progression, and median survival without transplant is less than one year, though spontaneous resolution can occur in patients with CBL mutations or germline PTPN11 mutations. Treatment is curative only with HSCT; before transplant, asymptomatic patients may simply be observed, or disease burden may be decreased with cytoreductive therapy.
keypoints: JMMoL is a rare aggressive childhood MDS/MPN overlap neoplasm
Diagnosis needs all category 1 clinical features, plus 1 category 2 molecular criterion, or 2 category 3 features if category 2 is negative
Category 2 mutations are PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, NF1, or germline CBL with loss of heterozygosity
Pathogenesis is hyperactive RAS signaling; median survival without HSCT is under one year
HSCT is the only curative treatment; CBL or germline PTPN11 mutations can allow spontaneous resolution
keypoint_voiceover: To summarize JMMoL. It is a rare, aggressive childhood MDS-MPN overlap disease. Diagnosis requires all the mandatory clinical features, plus either one molecular hit among PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, NF1, or germline CBL, or, lacking that, at least two supportive hematologic features. Pathogenesis is driven by hyperactive RAS signaling, prognosis is poor with median survival under a year without transplant, though CBL or germline PTPN11 mutations can spontaneously resolve, and HSCT remains the only curative treatment.
